newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Paris Club members to cut Zambia debt 67 percent.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club members to cut Zambia debt 67 percent.

text.p: Zambia's debts to the Paris Club group of donor nations are to be cut by 67 percent following success in implementing economic reforms, Finance Minister Ronald Penza said on Wednesday.

The Paris Club -- Austria, Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Britain and the United States -- will cut the debt after the International Monetary Fund's endorsement of Zambia's economic performance, he said in a statement.

"The successful outcome of last Friday's mid-term (IMF) review will now pave the way for Zambia to formalise the agreement which was reached last year with the Paris Club for a 67 percent reduction in Zambia's external debt service obligations to Paris Club members," Penza said.
Penza said key achievements included reducing inflation to the lowest annual level in eight years at 35 percent, and 6.5 percent economic growth in 1996.
Other achievements included an increase in social sector spending at 34.5 percent and progress in privatisation.
But Penza said Zambia needed to cut further its external debt, which soaks up vast resources.
"On a per capita basis, Zambia is currently still spending four times as much on external debt service as it does on improving the health of its citizens," he said.
Total external debt stands at $6.38 billion and the country aims to win further relief from a recently approved debt initiative for heavily indebted poor countries, for which it is eligible.
